papers.title: Text-to-Speech Bahasa Melayu Dialek Lubuk Kandis Menggunakan Metode VITS
papers.abstract: The existence of numerous regional languages in Indonesia reflects the country's cultural richness, with their historical distribution forming various dialects. One of them is the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect. To support the preservation and dissemination of this language, this study applies speech synthesis technology in the form of Text-to-Speech (TTS) to generate speech output for the Lubuk Kandis dialect. A dataset consisting of 500 daily activity sentences was recorded by a native speaker of Lubuk Kandis and validated by a local linguistic expert. The Variational Inference with Adversarial Learning for End-to-End Text-to-Speech (VITS) method was adopted to produce speech output that resembles natural human voice. The evaluation used the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) test involving five respondents and resulted in an average score of 4.72, indicating that the generated speech falls into the good category. These findings demonstrate that the VITS method is effective in synthesizing natural and intelligible speech for the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect, providing potential support for the preservation of regional languages.
reasons: Speech Generation, Recognition & Dialogue: speech synthesis, text-to-speech

papers.title: SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform
papers.abstract: Sign language is an essential means of communication for individuals with hearing and speech impairments. However, communication barriers often arise between sign language users and people who are unfamiliar with sign language. To address this challenge, this paper presents a SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform that uses computer vision and deep learning techniques to recognize hand gestures and convert them into understandable text. The proposed system is developed using Python, Flask, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and a trained machine learning model. It provides multiple detection methods, including image-based detection, video-based detection, multi-image processing, and real-time webcam recognition. The system also incorporates interactive learning features such as sign language practice, tutorials, a chatbot, progress tracking, history, and analytics to support continuous learning. Additionally, an administrative panel enables administrators to manage users, tutorials, detection history, and application settings. The system processes hand landmarks and extracts relevant features to identify corresponding signs and display the predicted results through a user-friendly web interface. By integrating sign recognition with learning and progress-monitoring facilities, the proposed application aims to improve accessibility, support sign language education, and reduce communication barriers. The system demonstrates the potential of combining computer vision, deep learning, and web technologies to develop an interactive and accessible sign language recognition platform

Mr. Sahil Sharma, Mr. Vaibhav Sahadeo Korde

papers.title: Audio Analysis and Symbolic Music Note Generation
papers.abstract: This report documents an analysis of a short trumpet recording, working through the full pipeline fromraw waveform to a playable MIDI file and, eventually, engraved sheet music. I used the Fast FourierTransform (FFT) to look at the recording's overall spectral content and a Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) spectrogram to see how that content changed over time. The pYIN algorithm provided a frame-by-frame estimate of the fundamental frequency (f0), which, combined with peak-picking on the staticFFT spectrum, was used to identify musical notes. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), spectral centroid, spectral bandwidth, and a chromagram were also extracted to characterize the recording'stimbre and harmonic content.The f0 contour was grouped into fifteen discrete note events with defined start times, end times, and durations, which were then written out as a MIDI file using mido and imported into GarageBand toproduce sheet music. The pipeline worked end-to-end, but it was not clean: the f0 estimate trackedclose to a single low pitch for much of the clip even as the note table shows a wider melodic range, shortnotes near the 0.1-second mark were borderline between real events and tracking noise, and the last~1.5 seconds of the recording — mostly breath and decay rather than a clear pitch — still registered as asustained F4. These issues, and what might fix them, are discussed in Sections 4 and 5.
reasons: Music Foundation Models & Representations: symbolic music

models.card_text: --- language: - zh - en - ar - my - da - nl - fi - fr - de - el - he - hi - id - it - ja - km - ko - lo - ms - no - pl - pt - ru - es - sw - sv - tl - th - tr - vi license: apache-2.0 library_name: voxcpm tags: - text-to-speech - tts - multilingual - voice-cloning - voice-design - diffusion - audio pipeline_tag: text-to-speech --- # VoxCPM2 **VoxCPM2** is a tokenizer-free, diffusion autoregressive Text-to-Speech model — **2B parameters**, **30 languages**, **48kHz** audio output, trained on over **2 million hours** of multilingual speech data. [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-VoxCPM-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-ReadTheDocs-8CA1AF)](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live%20Playground-Demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenBMB/VoxCPM-Demo) [![Audio Samples](https://img.shields.io/badge/Audio%20Samples-Demo%20Page-green)](https://openbmb.github.io/voxcpm2-demopage) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-VoxCPM-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/KZUx7tVNwz) [![Lark](https://img.shields.io/badge/飞书群-VoxCPM-00D6B9?logo=lark&logoColor=white)](https://applink.feishu.cn/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=acds0b9d-23d8-4d7e-b696-d200f3e22a7f) [![MiniCPM Wiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/MiniCPM-Wiki-1677FF?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://modelbest.feishu.cn/wiki/UtWxwcERfiRIpIkBOjuc3h9tn1D) ## Highlights - 🌍 **30-Language Multilingual** — No language tag needed; input text in any supported language directly - 🎨 **Voice Design** — Generate a novel voice from a natural-language description alone (gender, age, tone, emotion, pace…); no reference audio required - 🎛️ **Controllable Cloning** — Clone any voice from a short clip, with optional style guidance to steer emotion, pace, and expression while preserving timbre - 🎙️ **Ultimate Cloning** — Provide reference audio + its transcript for audio-continuation cloning; every vocal nuance faithfully reproduced - 🔊 **48kHz Studio-Quality Output** — Accepts 16kHz reference; outputs 48kHz via AudioVAE V2's built-in super-resolution, no external upsampler needed - 🧠 **Context-Aware Synthesis** — Automatically infers appropriate prosody and expressiveness from text content - ⚡ **Real-Time Streaming** — RTF as low as ~0.3 on NVIDIA RTX 4090, and ~0.13 accelerated by [Nano-VLLM](https://github.com/a710128/nanovllm-voxcpm) - 📜 **Fully Open-Source & Commercial-Ready** — Apache-2.0 license, free for commercial use Supported Languages (30) Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Lao, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese Chinese Dialects: 四川话, 粤语, 吴语, 东北话, 河南话, 陕西话, 山东话, 天津话, 闽南话 ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install voxcpm ``` **Requirements:** Python ≥ 3.10, PyTorch ≥ 2.5.0, CUDA ≥ 12.0 · [Full Quick Start →](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html) ### Text-to-Speech ```python from voxcpm import VoxCPM import soundfile as sf model = VoxCPM.from_pretrained("openbmb/VoxCPM2", load_denoiser=False) wav = model.generate( text="VoxCPM2 brings multilingual support, creative voice design, and controllable voice cloning.", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("output.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Voice Design Put the voice description in parentheses at the start of `text`, followed by the content to synthesize: ```python wav = model.generate( text="(A young woman, gentle and sweet voice)Hello, welcome to VoxCPM2!", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("voice_design.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Controllable Voice Cloning ```python # Basic cloning wav = model.generate( text="This is a cloned voice generated by VoxCPM2.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", ) sf.write("clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) # Cloning with style control wav = model.generate( text="(slightly faster, cheerful tone)This is a cloned voice with style control.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("controllable_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Ultimate Cloning Provide both the reference audio and its exact transcript for maximum fidelity. Pass the same clip to both `reference_wav_path` and `prompt_wav_path` for highest similarity: ```python wav = model.generate( text="This is an ultimate cloning demonstration using VoxCPM2.", prompt_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", prompt_text="The transcript of the reference audio.", reference_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", ) sf.write("hifi_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Streaming ```python import numpy as np chunks = [] for chunk in model.generate_streaming(text="Streaming is easy with VoxCPM!"): chunks.append(chunk) wav = np.concatenate(chunks) sf.write("streaming.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ## Model Details | Property | Value | |---|---| | Architecture | Tokenizer-free Diffusion Autoregressive (LocEnc → TSLM → RALM → LocDiT) | | Backbone | Based on MiniCPM-4, totally 2B parameters | | Audio VAE | AudioVAE V2 (asymmetric encode/decode, 16kHz in → 48kHz out) | | Training Data | 2M+ hours multilingual speech | | LM Token Rate | 6.25 Hz | | Max Sequence Length | 8192 tokens | | dtype | bfloat16 | | VRAM | ~8 GB | | RTF (RTX 4090) | ~0.30 (standard) / ~0.13 (Nano-vLLM) | ## Performance VoxCPM2 achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on major zero-shot and controllable TTS benchmarks. See the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM#-performance) for full benchmark tables (Seed-TTS-eval, CV3-eval, InstructTTSEval, MiniMax Multilingual Test). ## Fine-tuning VoxCPM2 supports both full SFT and LoRA fine-tuning with as little as 5–10 minutes of audio: ```bash # LoRA fine-tuning (recommended) python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_lora.yaml # Full fine-tuning python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_all.yaml ``` See the [Fine-tuning Guide](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/finetuning/finetune.html) for full instructions. ## Limitations - Voice Design and Style Control results may vary between runs; generating 1–3 times is recommended to obtain the desired output. - Performance varies across languages depending on training data availability. - Occasional instability may occur with very long or highly expressive inputs. - **Strictly forbidden** to use for impersonation, fraud, or disinformation. AI-generated content should be clearly labeled. ## Citation ```bibtex @article{voxcpm2_2026, title = {VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning}, author = {VoxCPM Team}, journal = {GitHub}, year = {2026}, } @article{voxcpm2025, title = {VoxCPM: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Context-Aware Speech Generation and True-to-Life Voice Cloning}, author = {Zhou, Yixuan and Zeng, Guoyang and Liu, Xin and Li, Xiang and Yu, Renjie and Wang, Ziyang and Ye, Runchuan and Sun, Weiyue and Gui, Jiancheng and Li, Kehan and Wu, Zhiyong and Liu, Zhiyuan}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.24650}, year = {2025}, } ``` ## License Released under the [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) license, free for commercial use. For production deployments, we recommend thorough testing and safety evaluation tailored to your use case.

--- license: other license_name: fish-audio-community-license license_link: LICENSE base_model: fishaudio/drama-3 base_model_relation: quantized pipeline_tag: text-to-speech tags: - comfyui - text-to-speech - voice-cloning - fish-audio - drama-3 ---

Nodes on GitHub · All samples · Qwen3-ASR for the transcripts · The original model

**[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3)**, converted for the native ComfyUI nodes of **[ComfyUI-Drama3](https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-Drama3)**: a 35B text-to-speech model for voice cloning, dialogue and inline cues such as `[sighs]` or `[whispers]`, running **on cards from 8 GB**. 90% of the model is routed experts and each audio frame uses only 8 of the 256 in a layer, so the nodes keep the experts in system RAM and a cache of the ones in use on the GPU. Each file holds the whole model in one file; the codec is separate. Built with Fish Audio. ## Samples No real person is cloned here: the first three clone voices the model made up from a single line, the rest are voices it invents from the prompt alone. Drama 3 FP8, experts in RAM, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.9, top_k 30 (the nodes now default to top_k 0, as Fish Audio's Space does: top_k 30 made some takes fall silent and drop a sentence). **[More on the demo page →](https://pedromarinhodev.github.io/ComfyUI-Drama3/)** **Voice cloning**: the source clip, a voice the model made up from one line, then a new line in that voice > The lighthouse keeper climbed the last step, set her lantern on the sill, and watched the storm roll in across the bay. Somewhere below, a bell began to ring. **Inline cues** > [whispers] Don't move. I think it heard us. [pause] [sighs] Oh, it's only the cat. [laughs] You should have seen your face. **Two speakers** > <|speaker:0|> Did you remember the tickets?
> <|speaker:1|> [laughs] I thought you had them!
> <|speaker:0|> [sighs] Then we're watching the concert from the parking lot. **Five speakers**, no voices given: the model casts all five > <|speaker:0|> [dramatic dungeon master] You enter the dark cave. A dragon sleeps on a pile of gold.
> <|speaker:1|> [brave, too loud] I attack the dragon! … **Singing** > [singing, grand operatic] Oh toast, my golden toast, you're the bread I love the most! [singing softly] Crispy edges, warm and brown, finest slice in all the town. … **Portuguese** > [Brazilian football fan, building tension, Portuguese] Vai, vai, vai, vai! Ele passou por um, passou por dois, [shouting] olha o chute! … ## Files **Start with FP8**: it holds Fish Audio's own expert weights, byte for byte, next to the checkpoint's bf16 layers. The int8 file is the same size, measured as close to the original, and ran 14–17% faster than FP8 on an RTX 3090: the nodes turn FP8 experts into bf16 each time they run, while int8 experts run as int8. Take a smaller file when your system RAM is short of the FP8 file's ~48 GB. Every model file needs the codec. | File | Size | Experts | System RAM | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | [`drama3_fp8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_fp8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 38.6 GB | FP8, as Fish Audio ships them | ~48 GB | the original weights | | [`drama3_int8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_int8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 38.7 GB | int8 ConvRot | ~48 GB | faster than FP8 on the 3090; no silent take in 12 cloned test takes | | [`drama3_w6a8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_w6a8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 32.7 GB | W6A8 | ~40 GB | no silent take in 16 cloned test takes | | [`drama3_w4a8experts_bf16.safetensors`](drama3_w4a8experts_bf16.safetensors) | 24.6 GB | W4A8 | ~32 GB | falls silent more often with real voice clips | | [`drama3_codec.safetensors`](drama3_codec.safetensors) | 1.6 GB | | | the original codec, fp32 | ## Quick start 1. **Install the nodes**: clone [ComfyUI-Drama3](https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-Drama3) into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes` and restart ComfyUI. Nothing to `pip install`. 2. **Download** a model file into `models/diffusion_models` and `drama3_codec.safetensors` into `models/vae`. For transcripts, add `qwen3_asr_1.7b_bf16.safetensors` from [Qwen3-ASR-ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/PedroMarinhoDev/Qwen3-ASR-ComfyUI) to `models/asr`, and for the Drama 3 Editor's word-by-word captions, `qwen3_forced_aligner_0.6b_bf16.safetensors` from the same repository. ```bash hf download PedroMarinhoDev/Drama-3-ComfyUI drama3_fp8experts_bf16.safetensors --local-dir ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models hf download PedroMarinhoDev/Drama-3-ComfyUI drama3_codec.safetensors --local-dir ComfyUI/models/vae hf download PedroMarinhoDev/Qwen3-ASR-ComfyUI qwen3_asr_1.7b_bf16.safetensors --local-dir ComfyUI/models/asr hf download PedroMarinhoDev/Qwen3-ASR-ComfyUI qwen3_forced_aligner_0.6b_bf16.safetensors --local-dir ComfyUI/models/asr ``` 3. **Open the workflow** `example_workflows/drama3_voice_clone.json` from the pack, pick a few seconds of clean speech, write your text, run. 4. **Edit the take** (optional): the **Drama 3 Editor** node, in place of Decode, shows the take on a timeline with one track per voice and captions that follow the words; it shortens long pauses, spaces out lines that run into each other, flags lines that may have lost words, and cuts. For dialogue, give each speaker a voice: the voice in slot `voiceN` speaks for `<|speaker:N|>`. ## Requirements and speed | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA, 8 GB of VRAM or more with experts in RAM (tested: RTX 4090 and RTX 3090; 12 GB and 8 GB simulated on the 3090) | | System RAM | the model file plus ~8 GB | | ComfyUI | v0.40 or newer | Drama 3 makes 21.5 audio frames per second of speech, so 46 ms per frame is real time. Experts in RAM, a cloned voice, ~9 s of speech, prompt pass included, measured on 2026-10-15 with an Intel Core i9-14900K (the held rows on 2026-10-14). One frame at a time, decoding waits on the CPU: int8 runs at the same 69 ms per frame on both GPUs, and a CPU with slower cores adds to these times: | GPU | File | Expert cache | ms per frame | |---|---|---|---| | RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 ×8) | W4A8 | 16 GB | 52 | | RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 ×8) | int8 | 16 GB | 69 | | RTX 3090 (PCIe 4.0 ×8) | int8 | 16 GB | 69 | | RTX 3090 (PCIe 4.0 ×8) | FP8 | 16 GB | 84 | | RTX 3090 held to 12 GB | FP8 | automatic | 137 | | RTX 3090 held to 8 GB | FP8 | automatic | 214 | ## How these files were made From [fishaudio/drama-3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) with the pack's `tools/convert.py`: - **FP8**: the routed experts' FP8 bytes and 128×128 block scales copied unchanged, gate and up projections fused. - **int8 / W6A8 / W4A8**: the experts dequantized from FP8 in fp32 and requantized, in ComfyUI's comfy_kitchen formats: int8 ConvRot (per-channel int8 after a rotation in groups of 256), or 6-bit or 4-bit codebook weights with int8 activations; relative weight error 0.83%, 2.1% and 7.3%. - **Every file**: the attention, DeltaNet, shared-expert and codebook-decoder layers are the checkpoint's own bf16; the LM head keeps only the rows generation samples from (end of speech and the 4096 semantic codes). - **Codec**: Fish Audio's S2-Pro codec as shipped with Drama 3, weight norm folded in, fp32. Against Fish Audio's own PyTorch code, with the same frames forced, the main token's distribution differs by a KL of 0.004–0.008 nats with the FP8 and int8 files, the noise of bf16 arithmetic. ## License These Fish Audio Materials are licensed under the Fish Audio Community License, Version 1.0. Copyright © 39 AI, INC. All Rights Reserved. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). Free for research and non-commercial use, and for commercial use below USD 500k annual revenue; a hosted TTS service needs a separate license from Fish Audio. Don't use these files or their output to imitate the voice of an identifiable person without their consent, or to train or improve other speech models. **Built with Fish Audio.** This repository is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by Fish Audio.

# Kitten TTS 2 for audio.cpp

**Powered by Stellon Labs.**

Self-contained multilingual GGUF exports of KittenML/kitten-tts-2 weights at
revision `f2eee74f4467855ad58fe16f1fb7b7df473263fd`. Each file includes the default
S3 MeanFlow decoder, speaker encoders, tokenizer, and all 48 prepared voice entries.

Use an audio.cpp build containing the updated Kitten TTS 2 BF16/Q8/Q4 support.
The model family is `kitten_tts2`. Model-manager installations share
`models/kitten-tts2/`, with a distinct filename for each precision. Leave `kitten_tts2.weight_type` unset, or use
`native`, to preserve each file's stored precision. Inference needs no Python
or LibTorch installation.

## Downloads

**Q8 is the default and recommended package.** Q4 is experimental.

| File | LM body / embedding | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [kitten-tts2-bf16-multilingual.gguf](./kitten-tts2-bf16-multilingual.gguf) | BF16 / BF16 | 4,603,407,040 bytes |
| [kitten-tts2-q8-v2-multilingual.gguf](./kitten-tts2-q8-v2-multilingual.gguf) | Q8_0 / BF16 | 3,282,201,248 bytes |
| [kitten-tts2-q4-multilingual.gguf](./kitten-tts2-q4-multilingual.gguf) | Q4_0 / Q8_0 | 2,273,735,456 bytes |

Verify downloads with [SHA256SUMS](./SHA256SUMS). All three packages use standard
GGML tensor types. Their names describe LM storage; decoder and reference
components retain their original precision.

Q8 and Q4 preserve the supplied ternary body weights exactly. Q4 quantizes the
embedding directly from full BF16 to Q8_0, with about 0.44% relative L2 weight
error. This is a weight reconstruction measurement, not an audio quality score.
On CUDA, Q4 down projections load as BF16 to avoid non-finite computation,
adding about 483 MiB compared with retaining those projections as Q4.

## Speech and cloning

```sh
audiocpp_cli --family kitten_tts2 --model models/kitten-tts2/kitten-tts2-q8-v2-multilingual.gguf --backend cpu --threads 8 --task tts --voice-id Bruno --text "Hello from Kitten TTS 2." --out hello.wav
```

Use `--backend cuda` for a CUDA-enabled build. For custom voice cloning:

```sh
audiocpp_cli --family kitten_tts2 --model models/kitten-tts2/kitten-tts2-q8-v2-multilingual.gguf --backend cpu --threads 8 --task clon --voice-ref reference.wav --reference-text "The exact words in the reference recording." --text "The new words to say." --out cloned.wav
```

Cloning requires a 1–30 second reference recording and its transcript. Preset
synthesis needs no separate voice recordings. Output is mono 24 kHz.

The package includes 47 upstream presets and the `PreparedBruno` alias. Named
English voices include Bruno, Bella, Jasper and Luna. Language presets cover
Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish.
Choose a matching preset or reference clip for the target language. Generation
checks cover these ten languages including English; they do not establish
native-speaker pronunciation quality.

## Validation and limitations

CPU and NVIDIA CUDA synthesis and cloning are checked locally. Q4 remains
experimental: longer samples sometimes omitted words. Broader listening review
is needed before relying on it for long-form speech. File sizes do not describe
runtime RAM or VRAM requirements.

The default decoder is used in every export. Student decoders and the upstream
TL2/emb4 format are not included. Streaming and automatic reference transcription
are not supported. Write numbers and abbreviations as spoken words when needed.

## Sources and license

- Kitten weights: KittenML/kitten-tts-2, revision `f2eee74f4467855ad58fe16f1fb7b7df473263fd`.
- Default S3 decoder: ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo, revision `749d1c1a46eb10492095d68fbcf55691ccf137cd`.
- Speaker encoder: the Kitten-distributed speaker model, attributed upstream to pyannote/embedding.

Model materials retain the Stellon Labs Community License in [LICENSE](./LICENSE).
Bundled components retain their respective terms in [native/LICENSE](./native/LICENSE)
and [speaker/LICENSE](./speaker/LICENSE). See [NOTICE](./NOTICE) for attribution
and conversion details.

Conversion and native integration by **dignome**. Prepared with AI assistance
and validated locally.

# VoxCPM2-Ghana

**Author:** [Ghana Open AI](https://huggingface.co/ghanaopenai)

**Supported by** [Ghana NLP](https://ghananlp.org)

Text-to-speech for six languages of Ghana: **Twi, Fante, Ewe, Dagbani, Dagaare and Ikposo**.
It is [VoxCPM2](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2) (2B parameters, 48 kHz output) fully
fine-tuned on the Ghana-recorded part of Google's [WAXAL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/WaxalNLP) speech dataset.

Write text in each language's normal spelling (ɛ, ɔ, ŋ, ʋ, ɣ, ʒ …). No phonetic conversion is needed.

## Quick start

**Try it:** [ghananlpcommunity/voxcpm2-ghana](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ghananlpcommunity/voxcpm2-ghana) (Space).

The easiest way to use it in code is the [voxcpm2-ghana](https://github.com/GhanaOpenAI/voxcpm2-ghana) package. It
has 83 built-in voices that you can listen to first: clean recordings from the model's own training data, kept in
[ghanaopenai/ghana-audio-prompts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ghanaopenai/ghana-audio-prompts). It also lets
you clone your own voice.

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/GhanaOpenAI/voxcpm2-ghana.git
voxcpm-ghana speakers --lang ewe --gender female
voxcpm-ghana speak "Akpe na wò, Mawu neyra wò." --speaker ewe-adult-female-1 -o hello.wav
```

```python
from voxcpm_ghana import GhanaTTS

tts = GhanaTTS()
wav = tts.speak("Me daase pii, Nyame nhyira wo.", speaker="twi-adult-female-1")
tts.save(wav, "twi.wav")

# Clone any voice from a clean 5–15 s recording (transcript optional)
wav = tts.speak("Akpe na wò.", ref_audio="my_voice.wav")
```

It also works directly with the `voxcpm` library like the base model:

```python
from voxcpm import VoxCPM
model = VoxCPM.from_pretrained("ghanaopenai/voxcpm2-ghana", load_denoiser=False)
wav = model.generate(text="Akpe na wò.", prompt_wav_path="ref.wav", prompt_text="<transcript of ref.wav>")
```

## Full-precision weights

The default (`main`) weights are bf16, the same format as the base VoxCPM2. The original fp32 weights for
step 7,000 are on the [`fp32` branch](https://huggingface.co/ghanaopenai/voxcpm2-ghana/tree/fp32), for
continued fine-tuning:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from voxcpm import VoxCPM

path = snapshot_download("ghanaopenai/voxcpm2-ghana", revision="fp32")
model = VoxCPM(voxcpm_model_path=path, enable_denoiser=False)
```

## Training data

The University of Ghana subsets of Google WAXAL (CC-BY-4.0). The 16 kHz mono audio was resampled from the 44.1 kHz originals; clips over 30 s were dropped.

| WAXAL subset | Language | Speech | Train hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aka_asr` | Akan (Twi and Fante) | many speakers, describing pictures | 55.0 |
| `dag_asr` | Dagbani | many speakers | 77.0 |
| `dga_asr` | Dagaare | many speakers | 83.3 |
| `ewe_asr` | Ewe | many speakers | 79.4 |
| `kpo_asr` | Ikposo | many speakers | 82.0 |
| `ewe_tts` | Ewe | 4 studio voices, read speech | 2.9 |
| `fat_tts` | Fante | 4 studio voices, read speech | 2.3 |
| `twi_tts` | Twi | 4 studio voices, read speech | 2.5 |
| **Total** | | 71,210 clips | **384.4** |

The unlabelled WAXAL audio (no transcripts) was not used.

## Training

- Full fine-tune (not LoRA) with the authors' own script, `scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py` from [OpenBMB/VoxCPM](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM), using the stock `voxcpm_v2` config.
- 1× NVIDIA H200, bf16. Learning rate 1e-5 with 500 warm-up steps, effective batch 32, gradient clipping 1.0.
- This release is **step 7,000** (about 3 epochs). Training ran to step 15,667. Validation audio loss levelled off after about 3k steps, and the stop-prediction loss started to overfit later on. In side-by-side listening tests on held-out sentences, step 7,000 sounded better than step 14,000 in every language.

| Step | Val `loss/diff` | Val `loss/stop` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (base VoxCPM2) | 0.890 | 0.091 |
| 3,000 | 0.846 | 0.022 |
| **7,000 (this model)** | **0.839** | **0.038** |
| 14,000 | 0.833 | 0.071 |

## Limitations

- Most training speech is crowd-sourced phone recordings of people describing pictures, so the model's own default voice can sound casual or slightly noisy. For the cleanest output, use one of the built-in voices (the cleanest training recordings, checked by ear) or a clean reference recording.
- Akan training data mixes Twi and Fante. Pick a Twi or Fante speaker to steer the dialect.
- Numbers, abbreviations and English words are read as written. Spell them out in the target language for best results.
- Not evaluated with automatic intelligibility metrics (no ASR exists yet for several of these languages). Quality was judged by listening.

## Responsible use

Voice cloning can be misused. Only clone voices with the speaker's consent, and don't use this model to impersonate real people or to deceive.

## Credits

- **Base model:** VoxCPM2 by OpenBMB (Apache-2.0).
- **Data:** Google WAXAL, Ghanaian language subsets collected by the University of Ghana (CC-BY-4.0).
- **Fine-tuning:** [Ghana Open AI](https://huggingface.co/ghanaopenai).

Built by [Ghana Open AI](https://huggingface.co/ghanaopenai), supported by [Ghana NLP](https://ghananlp.org).

# S2 Pro — GGUF

> **ALPHA — EXPERIMENTAL**
> The inference engine ([s2.cpp](https://github.com/rodrigomatta/s2.cpp)) is an early-stage, community-built project. Expect rough edges and breaking changes. Not production-ready.

GGUF-quantized weights of [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://fish.audio), a high-quality multilingual text-to-speech model with voice cloning support, packaged for local inference with [s2.cpp](https://github.com/rodrigomatta/s2.cpp) — a pure C++/GGML engine with no Python dependency.

> **License:** Fish Audio Research License — free for research and non-commercial use. Commercial use requires a separate license from Fish Audio. See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md) and [fish.audio](https://fish.audio).

---

## Files

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `s2-pro-f16.gguf` | 9.3 GB |
| `s2-pro-q8_0.gguf` | 5.3 GB |
| `s2-pro-q6_k.gguf` | 4.3 GB |
| `s2-pro-q5_k_m.gguf` | 3.8 GB |
| `s2-pro-q4_k_m.gguf` | 3.4 GB |
| `s2-pro-q3_k.gguf` | 2.9 GB |
| `s2-pro-q2_k.gguf` | 2.4 GB |
| `tokenizer.json` | 12 MB |

All GGUF files contain both the transformer weights and the audio codec in a single file.

---

## Requirements

- GPU with Vulkan support (AMD/NVIDIA/Intel) **or** CPU with enough RAM
- [s2.cpp](https://github.com/rodrigomatta/s2.cpp) built from source (C++17 + CMake)

### VRAM guide

| VRAM | Recommended |
|---|---|
| ≥ 8 GB | `q8_0` |
| 6–8 GB | `q6_k` |
| 4–6 GB | `q5_k_m` |
| 3–4 GB | `q4_k_m` |
| < 3 GB | `q3_k` / `q2_k` (quality degrades) |
| CPU only | `q4_k_m` or lower (slow) |

---

## Quick start

```bash
# Clone and build s2.cpp
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/rodrigomatta/s2.cpp.git
cd s2.cpp
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DS2_VULKAN=ON
cmake --build build --parallel $(nproc)

# Download model files (example with huggingface-cli)
huggingface-cli download rodrigomt/s2-pro-gguf s2-pro-q6_k.gguf tokenizer.json --local-dir .

# Synthesize
./build/s2 \
  -m s2-pro-q6_k.gguf \
  -t tokenizer.json \
  -text "Hello, this is a test." \
  -v 0 \
  -o output.wav
```

### Voice cloning

```bash
./build/s2 \
  -m s2-pro-q6_k.gguf \
  -t tokenizer.json \
  -pa reference.wav \
  -pt "Transcript of the reference audio." \
  -text "Text to synthesize in that voice." \
  -v 0 \
  -o output.wav
```

Reference audio: 5–30 seconds, clean recording, WAV or MP3.

---

## Quantization

The GGUF files in this repository were re-quantized using a modified `llama-quantize` tool with improved quantization routines. 

---

## Model architecture

S2 Pro uses a **Dual-AR** architecture (~4.56B parameters total):

- **Slow-AR** — 36-layer Qwen3 transformer (4.13B params), GQA (32 heads / 8 KV heads), RoPE 1M base, persistent KV cache
- **Fast-AR** — 4-layer transformer (0.42B params) generating 10 acoustic codebook tokens per semantic step
- **Audio codec** — convolutional RVQ encoder/decoder (10 codebooks × 4096 entries)

---

## License

The model weights are licensed under the **Fish Audio Research License**.

- **Research and non-commercial use:** free under this license
- **Commercial use:** requires a separate written license from Fish Audio

# Drama 3 GGUF for audio.cpp

Built with Fish Audio.

Experimental native audio.cpp conversions of
[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3), prepared from
checkpoint revision `dd64a85cd82e9521f7202610ede97b367fc83946`.
All packages use the same trained model architecture and checkpoint.

**Standard GGML K-quants with mixed precision.** The packages use Q2_K,
Q3_K_S and Q4_K_S file profiles with pure expert banks and explicit precision
overrides. Routed expert tensors use Q2_K, Q3_K and Q4_K storage respectively.
`backbone-8bit` means Q8_0 language-backbone matrices; `backbone-4bit` means
Q4_K matrices with a Q4_0 text embedding. The table below lists the precision overrides. Audio-tower matrices and waveform codec
weights remain FP16; audio-tower normalization and other retained FP32 vectors are unchanged.

## Files and precision

| Profile / file | Size | Routed experts | Routers / gates | Text embedding | Speech head | Other backbone matrices |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Q4 experts / Q8 backbone](./drama-3-backbone-8bit-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf) | 22.91 GiB | Q4_K | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 |
| [Q3 experts / Q8 backbone](./drama-3-backbone-8bit-experts-Q3_K_S.gguf) | 18.93 GiB | Q3_K | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 |
| [Q2 experts / Q8 backbone](./drama-3-backbone-8bit-experts-Q2_K.gguf) | 15.88 GiB | Q2_K | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 |
| [Q4 experts / Q4 backbone](./drama-3-backbone-4bit-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf) | 21.78 GiB | Q4_K | Q4_K | Q4_0 | Q4_K | Q4_K |
| [Q4 + FP32 routers](./drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf) | 22.97 GiB | Q4_K | FP32 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | Q8_0 |
| [Q4 + FP32 routers + BF16 embedding/head](./drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-BF16-embed-head-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf) | 23.87 GiB | Q4_K | FP32 | BF16 | BF16 | Q8_0 |

The Q3_K_S and Q4_K_S file profiles use pure expert banks: all 120 routed
expert projection banks have uniform Q3_K or Q4_K storage. Their storage-type
selection corresponds to a standard `--pure` K profile with explicit precision
overrides for the dense backbone, text embedding and audio components.
Architecture-specific higher-bit promotion heuristics are not applied; an
unmodified default llama.cpp preset can choose different types for some tensors.
See the standard converter's [pure and per-tensor options](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/quantize/quantize.cpp).
The native audio.cpp converter takes `--expert-type q3_k` or
`--expert-type q4_k`. The table above lists each component's actual storage type.

Q2, Q3 and Q4 are mixed quantizations. Q8_0 stores scaled 8-bit integer weights;
it is different from the FP8 representation of the original checkpoint's experts.
All packages retain FP16 audio-tower matrices and waveform codec weights. Backbone
and audio-tower normalization vectors remain FP32; codec normalization remains FP16. They embed the configuration, tokenizer, codec,
model contract and license, so inference does not require the original checkpoint
directory.

This repository distributes six standalone packages. All six retain the original
full-size speech head and work with the standard Drama 3 loader in current audio.cpp main.
Other quantizations can be prepared locally from the original checkpoint.

### FP32-router profiles

Both are **4-bit Q4_K_S expert profiles with mixed precision**. Their
filenames end in `Q4_K_S` so Hugging Face groups them under 4-bit in the
GGUF picker. The table above specifies each component's precision.

The two FP32-router files keep all 120 routed expert projection banks at **Q4_K**
and the other backbone matrices at **Q8_0**. Both restore the 40 expert routers and
40 shared-expert gates from the original checkpoint and store their values as FP32.
The BF16 profile additionally restores the original **BF16 text embedding and full speech head**.
The original router tensors were BF16; expanding those values into FP32 retains
them exactly and avoids Q8 rounding. These labels describe selected components
of a mixed-precision model. They do not describe an entirely FP32 or BF16 model.

Both files retain the complete 252,288-row `lm_head.weight` tensor. No compact-head
runtime changes or upstream pull request are needed to use these downloads.

* FP32 routers, Q8_0 text embedding/head: `drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf`
* FP32 routers, BF16 text embedding/head: `drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-BF16-embed-head-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf`

## Runtime compatibility

Drama 3 support is merged into [audio.cpp main](https://github.com/0xShug0/audio.cpp).
Build a current checkout with the `fish_drama3` backend enabled. Validation of the
two FP32-router packages used unmodified upstream commit
[`e065d66b`](https://github.com/0xShug0/audio.cpp/commit/e065d66b7aa70bb697e39b1e7a952197f017baef)
on Windows CPU and CUDA, with no compact-head patch.

Follow the [Windows build and server instructions](https://github.com/0xShug0/audio.cpp/blob/main/docs/models/fish_drama3.md).
The runtime is a native C++ CLI and HTTP server. No Python inference process is required.
Releases from before Drama 3 was merged do not include this backend.

These packages have GGUF architecture `audiocpp` and require its model loader
and embedded resource contract. Stock audio.cpp builds without the Drama 3 port
and general-purpose GGUF text-model runtimes cannot run this architecture.

The port implements offline and streaming speech, voice references, speaker and
event directions, long-form chunking and continuation/edit history through take
artifacts. It remains experimental.

## Run with a compatible audio.cpp build

Download either new precision profile directly, then pass its path with `--model`.
A runtime package catalogue may still list only the original four download presets.

```powershell
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with huggingface_hub hf download Jmica/Drama-3-GGUF `
  drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf --local-dir models/Drama-3-GGUF
```

For the BF16 embedding/head profile, substitute `drama-3-backbone-8bit-F32-routers-BF16-embed-head-experts-Q4_K_S.gguf`.

Example using Q2 experts and the tested smaller-memory offload configuration:

```powershell
.\audiocpp_cli.exe --task tts --family fish_drama3 --backend cuda `
  --mode streaming --model .\drama-3-backbone-8bit-experts-Q2_K.gguf `
  --text 'A quick test of Drama Three.' --max-tokens 500 --seed 123 --threads 8 `
  --session-option fish_drama3.cpu_expert_layers=8 `
  --session-option fish_drama3.context_length=2048 --out speech.wav
```

For the original four files, the tested lower-memory configurations use 24 CPU expert layers with Q4 experts,
12 with Q3 experts, 8 with Q2 experts, or 20 with Q4 backbone. These are suggested
starting configurations, rather than enforced memory limits. Host RAM is needed
for the offloaded expert banks; model file size does not equal required VRAM.

The configurations were exercised on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with 96 GB VRAM,
CUDA 12.8, Windows and eight CPU threads. Physical 16 GB and 24 GB GPUs have
not been tested. Increasing context length or adding longer references/history
increases memory use.

For cloning, supply `--voice-ref reference.wav` and
`--request-option 'reference_text=The reference transcript.'`.
For editing, pass a previously returned `drama3_take` artifact through the
library/API, or saved take JSON through `previous_takes_file`.

## Validation limits

English speech, reference-conditioned cloning, streaming, long-form output and
continuation/edit artifacts were exercised locally. Quantized expert tensor
types and independent small-model math controls were also checked.

The two full-head FP32-router packages were checked for offline and streaming
generation on unmodified upstream CPU/CUDA builds. Their unchanged tensor payloads
were compared byte-for-byte with the source package, and restored weights were
checked against the tested precision variants and original checkpoint. The
layout change preserves the same trained weight values for all speech-token rows.

Earlier blind listening comparisons used compact-head versions of these precision
profiles. Those preferences alone do not establish that either full-head profile
has better voice quality or more reliable stage-direction delivery. Higher precision
is not a guarantee of better individual takes.

Emotion and nonverbal directions are not consistently reliable. Some tagged
takes produce prolonged reactions, omit dialogue or reach the generation cap.
This occurred with the original Q4-expert package as well as smaller variants.
The Q3 offload profile omitted dialogue after laughter in one tagged test, and a
Q2 long-form trial with heavier CPU offload reached the cap; the documented Q2
eight-layer offload profile completed that long-form case.

These checks do not establish perceptual parity with the original checkpoint,
consistent emotion delivery or broad multilingual quality. Transcript checks
verify words, rather than voice similarity or acting quality. Seeds reproduce a
take within the same execution configuration; changing quantization or offload
placement can change the sampled audio. The full-head FP32-router profiles use
more memory than their compact experimental counterparts; the BF16 embedding/head
profile also uses more memory than the original Q4/Q8 file.

## Conversion

The converter reconstructs the scaled FP8 experts with their original
128-by-128 scales and packs their projections into three-dimensional banks.
The native GGUF converter applies the chosen expert, backbone and embedding
weight types, folds codec weight normalization and embeds the runtime resources.
Expert banks remain quantized during native execution.

The converter exposes separate expert, backbone and embedding precision options.
Conversion uses CPU dependencies managed with uv. The new FP32-router profiles
restore router values directly from the original checkpoint; the BF16 profile
also restores the original text embedding and full output head. They retain
the remaining quantized payloads and the standard full-head tensor names/shapes.
The default conversion example below creates an ordinary expert/backbone profile;
it does not perform these additional original-weight restorations.

With a compatible port checkout and native GGUF converter, download the original
checkpoint and choose the desired precision. For example, to prepare Q5 experts:

```powershell
uv run tools/community_models/convert_fish_drama3.py `
  --checkpoint .\drama-3 --output .\drama3-f16-local.gguf `
  --quantized-output .\drama-3-backbone-8bit-experts-Q5_K.gguf `
  --gguf-tool .\audiocpp_gguf.exe `
  --expert-type q5_k --backbone-type q8_0 --embedding-type q8_0
```

The converter creates a local FP16 intermediate of approximately 68.2 GiB before
producing the runnable package. It can be reused for another precision through
`--input-gguf` instead of `--output`. The intermediate is not distributed here.

The model materials and these conversions are subject to the Fish Audio Community
License, Version 1.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE) for the original
terms, required attribution and description of modifications. This repository
is an independent conversion of Fish Audio Drama 3.
